paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Ten men got the same healing, and only one of them turned around. Jesus said to the ten, "Go, show yourselves to the priests," and as they were on their way, they were cleansed (Luke 17:14). The gift was the same for every one of them, but one man let it change where he walked.

Now watch what Jesus asks: "Were not all ten cleansed? Where then are the other nine?" (Luke 17:17). I don't think He's counting heads. I think He cares that the one who came back was praising God in a loud voice and fell facedown at His feet (Luke 17:15-16). Thanks is a way of looking at Jesus and saying, "You did this." And the one who did it was a Samaritan, a foreigner, so nobody gets to say they're too far outside to praise Him.

Then Jesus says to him, "Rise and go; your faith has made you well!" (Luke 17:19). So here's my question for you, friend. What has God already done for you that you've been hurrying past on the way to your next thing? I spent years in a junk drawer, and now I've got a cookie planet and a bakery, and I STILL have mornings where I'm halfway through the first batch before I say thank you. Go back, like that man did. Say it out loud, and say it LOUD.
